raw_response:
I’m farming 20 mu, and with some people in my family working off-farm, I can’t make the plan too labor-heavy or too risky. I’ve done this a long time, so I mostly follow what has worked on my land and what I see in the village. This year I’ll keep the main part in wheat-maize because that’s still the safest income, and I’ll keep some land in stevia because it brings cash if the stand is good. Since irrigation from the well costs money, I won’t water blindly, but I also won’t let the crop get hurt at the key stages. For fertilizer, I usually do a bit more than the bare minimum because if wheat or maize goes yellow, yield loss hurts more than spending a little extra on urea.

For the land, I’ll put 14 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize, and 6 mu into stevia. Wheat is already in the field for this year, so from April 18, 2026 I’m mainly thinking about topdressing, irrigation, and then getting maize in quickly right after wheat harvest. Stevia needs more hand work, so I won’t plant too much of it since family labor is limited. I want a steady year, not a fancy one: enough fertilizer to hold yield, enough water at the important time, and no big cash gamble.
